core_obligations: Given an R-module map alpha from N restricted to M, define alpha' from N to Hom_R(S, M) by sending n to the map s to alpha(s n) (proof lines 2720-2722).
Given an S-module map beta from N to Hom_R(S, M), define beta' from N restricted to M by n to beta(n)(1) (proof lines 2722-2724).
The two constructions are inverse to each other; the author states this step explicitly as omitted (proof line 2725).
proof_roadmap: Write both directions of the adjunction on elements, using the evaluation at 1 for the reverse direction (proof lines 2719-2724).
Leave the verification that the two are mutually inverse to the reader, as the author does (proof line 2725).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S the lemma states that restriction of scalars from S-modules to R-modules is left adjoint to the functor taking M to Hom_R(S, M) (statement lines 2708-2717). The proof writes both directions of the claimed bijection on elements: an R-module map alpha gives alpha'(n)(s) = alpha(s n), and an S-module map beta gives beta'(n) = beta(n)(1) (proof lines 2719-2724). The only step not written out is the mutual-inverse verification, which the author explicitly marks as omitted and which is a routine computation with the two displayed formulas; the count therefore rests on the two constructions, which are fully given. H2.
